question: What happens if an AED is accidentally used on someone whose heart is beating normally?

options.A: The heart will instantly stop due to the excess electrical current
options.B: The device will analyze the rhythm and refuse to deliver a shock
options.C: The machine will automatically start delivering CPR compressions
options.D: The internal battery of the device will permanently burn out

explanation: Don't worry, AEDs are very smart! They scan the heart first and will block any shock if the heart rhythm is normal. They won't harm a healthy beat. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h2)

question: In Nigeria, which setting usually records the lowest fertility rates?

options.A: Rural farming villages
options.B: Remote agrarian settlements
options.C: Urban centers
options.D: Nomadic pastoral communities

explanation: Correct! City dwellers often have smaller family sizes due to higher living costs and better access to school and family planning. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h4)

question: What special shape helps red blood cells squeeze through tiny blood vessels and carry plenty of oxygen?

options.A: Biconcave disc shape
options.B: Spherical amoeboid form
options.C: Rod-like crystalline structure
options.D: Presence of multiple nuclei

explanation: You nailed it! Their unique biconcave shape (flattened donuts without holes) gives them a massive surface area and makes them super flexible to squeeze through tight spots. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T1#GNS311_U2_T1_h4)

question: What symptom is most characteristic of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD)?

options.A: Chronic constipation
options.B: Severe right shoulder pain
options.C: Heartburn
options.D: Projectile vomiting of blood

explanation: You've got it! Heartburn—that burning discomfort right behind your breastbone caused by acid irritation—is the classic hallmark of GORD. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is a key nursing check to perform after a patient receives IV contrast dye?

options.A: Measuring hourly urine output to confirm total bladder atrophy
options.B: Monitoring for delayed allergic reactions like rash, itching, or breathing difficulty
options.C: Checking for immediate loss of hair color around the injection site
options.D: Assessing for sudden paralysis in the lower extremities

explanation: Allergic reactions to contrast dye can sometimes pop up hours later. Always keep an eye out for hives, itching, or any trouble breathing. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h7)

question: What usually triggers the body to develop secondary polycythaemia?

options.A: An autoimmune attack on bone marrow
options.B: An inherited defect in the platelets
options.C: Sudden heavy blood loss from injury
options.D: Chronic low oxygen levels in tissues

explanation: Spot on! When body tissues are short on oxygen over time, the body panics and pumps out more red blood cells to help. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T8#GNS311_U2_T8_h2)

question: Once an expectorant thins out the respiratory mucus, what helps sweep it up toward the throat?

options.A: They absorb the excess fluid so the lungs stay completely dry
options.B: They dissolve the chemical bonds holding the phlegm together
options.C: They sweep the loosened mucus upward toward the throat
options.D: They produce more thick mucus to trap remaining dust particles

explanation: Meet the cilia—tiny hair-like structures in your airways that wave together like a stadium crowd to push that loosened mucus right up and out! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h2)

question: What are individual and psychological causes of conflict mostly rooted in?

options.A: The official hospital building blueprint and layout
options.B: Government policies regarding nurse salaries
options.C: The exact number of beds available in the ward
options.D: Personal values, perceptions, and individual goals

explanation: These triggers come from within each person—how we view situations, what we value most, and what we personally want to achieve. [learn more](GST321_U5_T2#GST321_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is your very first action if a patient's chest tube accidentally disconnects from the drainage unit?

options.A: Apply tight adhesive tape all around the open tubing end
options.B: Clamp the chest tube securely near the insertion site
options.C: Submerge the end of the tube in sterile water
options.D: Lower the patient flat onto their back in bed

explanation: Quick thinking! Putting the tube tip in sterile water instantly creates a temporary seal and keeps air from rushing into the chest. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h7)

question: What does mutual respect mean within a healthcare team?

options.A: Remaining silent during ward rounds to save time
options.B: Working only with people who share your exact profession
options.C: Valuing the unique expertise of every team member
options.D: Agreeing with every decision the senior doctor makes

explanation: Exactly! Whether you are a nurse, doctor, or pharmacist, respecting each other's training and input creates a wonderful, safe environment for everyone. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h2)

question: Which muscle group helps guide the baby's head to rotate internally inside the pelvis?

options.A: The quadriceps femoris
options.B: The levator ani muscles
options.C: The external sphincter muscles
options.D: The abdominal wall muscles

explanation: You're doing great! The sloping levator ani muscles of the pelvic floor act like a slide, gently guiding the baby's head to turn. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h4)

question: What is the oily substance produced by sebaceous glands called?

options.A: Keratin
options.B: Sweat
options.C: Melanin
options.D: Sebum

explanation: Sebaceous glands secrete sebum, an oily substance that conditions the skin and hair. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why do modern clinical guidelines prefer Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) over traditional sharp metal curettage?

options.A: MVA is associated with less pain, lower complication rates, and quicker recovery
options.B: Sharp curettage instruments are too expensive for most developing nations
options.C: MVA completely eliminates the need for any pre-procedure pain medication
options.D: Sharp curettage requires general anesthesia in an operating theatre every time

explanation: You nailed it! MVA is gentler on the uterine lining and poses lower risks of perforation compared to sharp metal curettage. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h3)

question: What is the main difference between normal (physiological) and abnormal (pathological) moulding?

options.A: Physiological moulding is normal and reversible, while pathological moulding involves excessive, damaging forces
options.B: Physiological moulding only happens in premature babies, whereas pathological moulding happens at term
options.C: Pathological moulding causes soft swelling while physiological moulding causes hard ridges
options.D: Pathological moulding involves bone fractures and permanent shape changes

explanation: Spot on! Normal moulding happens in almost every birth and goes away on its own. Pathological moulding comes from extreme, harsh pressure that can cause harm. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h2)

question: Why is long-term, daily use of sleeping pills generally discouraged for chronic insomnia?

options.A: They stop working entirely after a single night and never help again.
options.B: They automatically cause permanent total blindness within six months of use.
options.C: They interfere with normal digestion by destroying all intestinal flora.
options.D: Patients quickly develop tolerance and physical dependence, and underlying issues remain unaddressed.

explanation: Pills tend to lose their punch over time because the body gets used to them (tolerance), and they only mask symptoms without fixing the root cause of the sleep trouble. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h7)

question: What is the main cause of inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Vitamin deficiencies during pregnancy
options.B: Genetic mutations passed down from parents
options.C: Severe bacterial infections in early childhood
options.D: Acute physical trauma to the central nervous system

explanation: You've got this! These conditions happen because of faulty genes handed down in families, which gradually break down body tissues over time. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h1)

question: How should a scrubbed nurse enter the operating room after finishing their scrub?

options.A: Back through the door to keep hands safe and away from clothing
options.B: Ask an unscrubbed colleague to open the door and pull them in
options.C: Push the door open while keeping hands high near the face
options.D: Turn sideways and slide through a narrow opening

explanation: Backing in ensures your front and clean hands don't accidentally brush against the door or your scrubs. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary tool nurses use to map out a family health history across generations?

options.A: A Punnett square
options.B: A blood glucose log
options.C: A genogram
options.D: A karyotype chart

explanation: A genogram is a visual family tree that helps nurses map inherited diseases and health patterns across generations. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h7)

question: How would you describe an 'asymptomatic carrier' to a fellow nursing student?

options.A: An individual who is currently experiencing severe symptoms of disease
options.B: A person who carries a pathogen without showing any signs of illness
options.C: A patient who has fully recovered and no longer sheds any germs
options.D: A healthcare worker who always wears proper personal protective equipment

explanation: Asymptomatic means no symptoms! They carry the germ around and feel totally fine, which is why infection control can be tricky. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T82#GNS214_U1_T82_h2)

question: A clinic audit reveals low uptake of post-abortion contraception among discharged PAC patients. What is the best quality improvement response for the nursing team?

options.A: Discharge patients immediately without discussing family planning options
options.B: Stop offering all abortion complication treatments until rates improve
options.C: Blame patients for failing to request birth control during their emergency
options.D: Review and strengthen same-day contraceptive counseling and supply availability

explanation: Brilliant! Spotting this gap lets the team fix counseling issues and make sure supplies are ready before discharge. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h8)

question: Why would a person die from a minor infection if they had no inflammatory response?

options.A: The liver would immediately stop producing essential proteins
options.B: Blood pressure would drop too low to sustain life
options.C: The body could not isolate and destroy invading germs
options.D: Red blood cells would stop carrying oxygen to tissues

explanation: Inflammation is the critical defense mechanism that walls off and eliminates harmful agents in the body. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h1)

question: How does the strict criminalization of abortion in Nigeria directly affect patient health outcomes?

options.A: It encourages traditional healers to adopt modern sterile surgical techniques
options.B: It guarantees that all post-abortion patients receive free government care
options.C: It forces patients to seek secretive care, leading to dangerous treatment delays
options.D: It completely eliminates the practice of illegal pregnancy terminations

explanation: Because of fear of arrest, women often hide what they've done and only come to the hospital when complications become life-threatening. Compassionate, confidential nursing care can help break down this fear! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h2)

question: How are direct-acting smooth muscle relaxants different from anticholinergics?

options.A: They completely destroy the nerve supply to the intestines
options.B: They stimulate more acetylcholine release to tire out the gut
options.C: They act directly on muscle tissue rather than blocking nerve signals
options.D: They only work on the skeletal muscles of the limbs

explanation: Instead of messing with nerve messages, direct-acting drugs go straight to the muscle fibers and tell them to chill out locally. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h2)

question: When is emergency surgery absolutely necessary for a patient with a small intestinal problem?

options.A: When the patient experiences mild cramping after eating dairy products
options.B: When routine blood tests show a slightly elevated white blood cell count
options.C: When signs of bowel strangulation, ischemia, or perforation appear
options.D: When the patient is diagnosed with mild celiac disease

explanation: If a part of the bowel loses its blood supply (ischemia) or bursts (perforation), it's a critical emergency requiring immediate surgery. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h7)

question: Which licensing requirement must a tele-nurse always meet when caring for remote clients?

options.A: Holding a valid license in the location where the patient is physically located
options.B: Having a license from any country as long as the nurse has a smartphone
options.C: Possessing a special international internet communication permit
options.D: Registering only with the hospital administration board

explanation: Regulatory bodies require nurses to be legally licensed in the specific jurisdiction where the patient receives the care. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h4)

question: How do patients dealing with heavy stress often present themselves in the clinic?

options.A: With sudden weight gain and lower blood pressure
options.B: With visible joy and high energy levels
options.C: With physical complaints like headaches, insomnia, and body pains
options.D: With enhanced memory and sharp focus

explanation: Emotional stress loves to hide in physical symptoms. When patients can't sleep or have endless body aches, stress is often the culprit! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why are peer educators so effective in adolescent health programs?

options.A: They are authorized to write prescriptions for antibiotics
options.B: Peer educators have medical degrees from universities
options.C: Young people often relate better to individuals in their own age group
options.D: Adults refuse to talk to anyone under twenty years old

explanation: Exactly! Teens share the same language and experiences, making peer educators trusted messengers who can easily connect with them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h7)

question: What kind of germs usually require contact precautions on the ward?

options.A: Vector-borne malaria parasites
options.B: Multi-drug resistant organisms
options.C: Airborne measles virus particles
options.D: Waterborne fungal spore clusters

explanation: You got it! Germs that laugh at common antibiotics love to hitch a ride on hands and hospital equipment, so we use strict contact precautions to keep them from spreading. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h3)

question: What is the most popular theory explaining how endometriosis starts in the first place?

options.A: Congenital uterine absence
options.B: Retrograde menstruation
options.C: Lymphatic vessel blockage
options.D: Primary ovarian failure

explanation: Retrograde menstruation is like a traffic mix-up where menstrual blood flows backward through the fallopian tubes and into the pelvis instead of leaving the body. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T21#GNS216_U5_T21_h2)

question: What is the main difference between emission and ejaculation?

options.A: Emission is controlled by parasympathetic nerves, while erection is sympathetic
options.B: Emission involves only the testes, while ejaculation involves the prostate
options.C: Emission moves fluid into the urethra, while ejaculation expels it outward
options.D: Emission happens before puberty, while ejaculation occurs only in adulthood

explanation: Spot on! Emission gathers and moves the fluid into the upper urethra, while ejaculation uses muscle contractions to push it completely out of the body. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of decentralising decisions down to frontline ward managers?

options.A: Complete standardisation of every hospital procedure
options.B: Faster response times to daily operational challenges on the ward
options.C: Lower salaries for all categories of nursing staff
options.D: Elimination of all policies set by top hospital administration

explanation: You got it! Letting ward leaders solve local problems on the spot means they don't have to wait around for approval from distant executives. [learn more](GST321_U1_T9#GST321_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why is local anesthetic WITHOUT epinephrine typically chosen for a skin snip?

options.A: Epinephrine causes severe systemic hypertension

options.C: Local anesthetics cannot be mixed with epinephrine under any rule
options.D: Vasoconstriction can interfere with parasite emergence from the tissue

explanation: Exactly. We want blood vessels to stay open so the tiny live parasites can easily crawl out of the skin sample into our liquid solution. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h3)

question: Which type of thread is used for outer skin stitches and needs to be taken out after a few days?

options.A: Absorbable suture
options.B: Non-absorbable suture
options.C: Catgut suture
options.D: Biodegradable thread

question: What is the main purpose of formative evaluation?

options.A: To give ongoing feedback to help you learn better
options.B: To check the school's financial budget
options.C: To pass the national licensing exam
options.D: To decide your final GPA for graduation

explanation: Formative evaluation is your friendly guide while you are still learning—it gives you feedback so you can improve before any big stakes exam. [learn more](GST321_U9_T2#GST321_U9_T2_h3)

question: What is a common sign that prompts a patient to suspect they might have a tapeworm?

options.A: Passing flat, white worm segments in the stool
options.B: Coughing up blood-stained sputum during the night
options.C: Noticing painful swelling in the lower limbs
options.D: Developing severe jaundice in the eyes and skin

explanation: Spot on! Patients often notice moving or detached worm segments (proglottids) in their toilet visits, which is usually what brings them to the clinic. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h4)

question: If a doctor tells you a patient has a mild stage of endometriosis, what does that tell you about her pain?

options.A: Pain levels increase in direct proportion to the amount of scar tissue
options.B: Surgical stage does not reliably predict the severity of the patient's pain
options.C: Patients with stage IV disease always experience the worst pelvic pain
options.D: Patients with stage I disease never require strong pain medication

explanation: Surprise! A patient with just a tiny bit of endometriosis can be in agonizing pain, while another with widespread patches might feel very little. Pain and staging don't always match. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T21#GNS216_U5_T21_h3)

question: Why is it important to check both physical health and mental status when assessing sexual problems?

options.A: Physical illnesses and emotional stress frequently interact to impair sexual function
options.B: Physical causes are always temporary while psychological ones are permanent
options.C: Medical insurance will not pay for treatment without both evaluations
options.D: Psychological causes can never be treated with medication

explanation: The body and mind work as a team. Good sexual health needs healthy blood vessels, steady hormones, and peace of mind all working together. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T27#GNS312_U1_T27_h3)

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: To ensure that hospitals charge the correct fees for admissions
options.B: To punish clinics that fail to treat enough patients each month
options.C: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy volunteer populations
options.D: To collect and analyze health data for early detection and planning

explanation: Exactly! Surveillance is like a early-warning radar. It tracks disease patterns continuously so health workers can spot trouble and plan ahead. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T76#GNS214_U1_T76_h3)

question: What is obstetric fistula?

options.A: The premature closing of the birth canal due to hormonal imbalances
options.B: A sudden infection of the outer reproductive organs during early pregnancy
options.C: An abnormal opening between the vagina and bladder or rectum caused by prolonged labor
options.D: A complete failure of the ovaries to release eggs during the menstrual cycle

explanation: Well done! When labor is blocked in a narrow pelvis, the crushed tissue dies, leaving a hole (fistula) that causes leaking of urine or stool. It's a devastating condition we work hard to prevent. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h2)

question: Which imaging test is safest and most commonly used to look at a pregnant woman's kidneys?

options.A: Renal ultrasound
options.B: Magnetic resonance angiography
options.C: Computed tomography scan
options.D: Abdominal x-ray with contrast

explanation: Ultrasound uses safe sound waves instead of radiation, making it completely harmless for both mum and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h4)

question: An item touches a patient's unbroken skin during a routine check-up. According to Spaulding's rules, what level of processing does it need?

options.A: Low-level disinfection
options.B: No processing is required
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: High-level disinfection

explanation: Items that only touch intact skin are non-critical and just need basic low-level disinfection between patients. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: How long should a child with watery diarrhea take zinc supplements according to IMNCI?

options.A: 1 month straight
options.B: 1 to 2 days
options.C: 10 to 14 days
options.D: Only on the first day

explanation: Giving zinc for 10 to 14 days helps repair the gut lining, restores lost nutrients, and protects the child from future tummy bugs. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T6#GNS215_U6_T6_h5)

question: What is a major nursing concern when an older adult has severe dental problems and missing teeth?

options.A: Increased likelihood of developing hypertension
options.B: Rapid cognitive decline within forty-eight hours
options.C: Immediate kidney failure due to poor digestion
options.D: Risk of malnutrition and difficulty chewing certain foods

explanation: When chewing hurts or is difficult, residents might skip healthy foods like meat and raw veggies unless their meals are specially prepared. You are learning great clinical foresight! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T13#GNS324_U5_T13_h6)

question: How soon can a woman theoretically start ovulating again after experiencing an abortion?

options.A: Never until she reaches menopause
options.B: Only after six full months have passed
options.C: Exactly one full year following treatment
options.D: As early as two weeks post-procedure

explanation: Fertility can bounce back remarkably fast after pregnancy termination, which is why birth control counseling must happen immediately during the PAC visit. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT usually needed when writing up a Chi-Square result?

options.A: The degrees of freedom
options.B: The p-value
options.C: The Chi-Square test statistic value
options.D: The exact blood pressure of participants

question: A patient living in a rural home with poor kitchen ventilation uses wood for daily cooking and now has a lasting cough. What is the best primary prevention advice?

options.A: Give them a course of strong oral antibiotics right away
options.B: Recommend using a quick-relief rescue inhaler every day
options.C: Order a chest X-ray to check for tuberculosis
options.D: Advise the family to switch to cleaner cooking fuel and improve kitchen airflow

explanation: Primary prevention stops the problem before it starts or worsens. Fixing indoor smoke exposure removes the root environmental trigger keeping that cough going! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h2)

question: You are planning a fun health talk on teenage reproductive health in a secondary school. What approach works best?

options.A: Flannel graphs depicting geriatric care management
options.B: Megaphone announcements in the central cattle market
options.C: Complex medical journals left in the staff room
options.D: Interactive drama or peer-led discussions

explanation: Teens connect best with lively, relatable methods like drama and chats with peers rather than reading boring medical documents. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses to get involved in community advocacy and health policies, alongside bedside care?

options.A: Adolescents never listen to advice given inside a hospital consultation room

options.C: Environmental and structural dangers cannot be fixed solely by treating individuals
options.D: Hospitals forbid nurses from performing any clinical procedures without laws

explanation: Brilliant! Treating injuries at the bedside is only half the battle. Community and policy changes are needed to tackle the root causes of danger in society. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T7#GNS312_U3_T7_h8)

question: Why would a doctor give a pregnant patient a tocolytic medication?

options.A: To provide effective pain relief during active labour
options.B: To induce rhythmic contractions for a post-dates labour
options.C: To temporarily halt premature uterine contractions
options.D: To prevent heavy bleeding immediately after delivery

explanation: Think of tocolytics as 'time-buys'—they relax the uterus to slow down early labor and give the baby more time to grow. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h5)

question: Which chemical is mainly responsible for opening up blood vessels during inflammation?

options.A: Pepsin
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Insulin

explanation: When tissues get hurt, mast cells release histamine. This chemical widens local blood vessels so helpful immune cells can rush to the rescue. [learn more](GST114_U4_T4#GST114_U4_T4_h4)

question: How is neonatal tetanus mainly diagnosed in clinical practice?

options.A: Routine magnetic resonance imaging scans
options.B: Positive blood culture results for the virus
options.C: Elevated white blood cell counts in urine
options.D: Physical examination and clinical history

explanation: You're doing great! Doctors and nurses diagnose it based on the baby's history—a normal birth followed by sudden stiffness, muscle spasms, and trouble feeding. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h5)

question: A Lassa fever patient's urine output drops to 15 mL/hour over two hours. What should you do first?

options.A: Document the finding as normal for viral infections and recheck in eight hours
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of plain water quickly
options.C: Stop all intravenous fluid infusions to give the kidneys a rest
options.D: Notify the doctor immediately and assess for developing kidney compromise

explanation: Low urine output is a red flag for acute kidney injury. Always report it promptly so the medical team can adjust care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h7)

question: A pregnant home-care patient has a single high blood pressure reading. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking all prescribed prenatal vitamins.
options.B: Immediately discharge the patient from home care services.
options.C: Perform serial blood pressure checks and notify the primary provider.
options.D: Wait until the scheduled monthly clinic visit to mention it.

question: Which of these statements about drug transfer across the placenta is FALSE?

options.A: Most fat-soluble drugs cross easily from mother to fetus
options.B: Medications taken during pregnancy can affect the unborn baby
options.C: The placenta serves as an impenetrable shield blocking all maternal drugs
options.D: Simple diffusion is a common way drugs cross the placenta

question: What factor makes the emotional and mental distress much worse for patients recovering from an unsafe abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: Social stigma and fear of legal consequences
options.B: Excessive availability of professional counselors
options.C: Mandatory psychological screening in government hospitals
options.D: Immediate support from community religious leaders

explanation: Fear of being arrested, judged, or rejected by loved ones forces many women to hide their pain and suffer all alone. As nurses, being a safe, listening ear makes all the difference. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h5)

question: A patient is brought to the emergency unit looking very restless, sweating profusely, and with a racing heart after taking an unknown substance. Which drug class is likely to blame?

options.A: Opioids
options.B: Sedative-hypnotics
options.C: Barbiturates
options.D: Stimulants

question: What is the medical term for the gradual loss of muscle mass and strength as people age?

options.A: Presbyopia
options.B: Sarcopenia
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Atherosclerosis

explanation: Spot on! Sarcopenia is the natural, progressive shrinking of skeletal muscle that happens as we grow older. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h4)

question: A community health nurse organizes a routine childhood vaccination drive at a local clinic. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: You got it! Giving immunizations protects healthy people from getting sick in the first place, which is primary prevention. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h3)

question: Why is the intracardiac injection route hardly ever used in modern hospitals anymore?

options.A: Patients refusing to allow needles near their chests
options.B: New laws making emergency heart surgery illegal
options.C: The high cost of manufacturing long needles

question: How many blood vessels are normally inside a healthy human umbilical cord?

question: Where exactly are sperm cells made inside the testes?

question: Why do nurses need to keep a close eye out when caring for women with sudden tummy pain in the emergency ward?

question: Which of these conditions is NOT a result of early embryonic developmental errors?

question: A baby is born limp, pale, and quiet after a home delivery. What should you do right away?

question: What is the main role of a healthcare proxy or durable power of attorney?

question: Which of these is a key part of active listening for a nurse leader?

question: What is the single most important and effective habit for stopping infections from spreading in any hospital or clinic?

question: What substance protects the blood vessels inside the umbilical cord from getting squeezed flat?

question: Which nursing intervention is essential for managing patients with hormone imbalances affecting fluid and electrolytes?

question: What is the main difference between an IDP and a refugee?

question: When a nurse gently pinches the skin to check hydration (skin turgor), which fibers in the dermis make the skin snap back?

question: Which meningeal layer wraps around the brain so tightly that it dips into every single groove and fold?

question: Why do community health nurses care about things like housing and clean water?

question: How do unit managers usually help with hospital budgeting?

question: In Nigerian public health, what does the acronym IDSR stand for?

question: What is the primary goal of a research critique?

question: Which part of the brainstem contains the main control hubs for heart rate and breathing rhythms?

question: Which of these common phrases should a nurse avoid saying to someone who is grieving?

question: What is the very first thing emergency responders do at an accident scene to protect a patient's spine?

question: Which statement best describes the role of multidisciplinary rounds in preventing complications?

question: A home health nurse notices signs of severe postpartum depression during a visit. What is the best collaborative action?

question: Why is regular self-reflection important for nurses working in post-abortion care?

question: Why must you check the expiration date on test strips before using them?

question: Which of these is NOT a main objective of the DRF system?

question: What is one of the biggest risks when wheeling a critical patient away for an advanced scan?

question: A 28-week pregnant client comes in complaining of a pounding headache and sudden blurry vision. What should pop into your head first?

question: How often should you check the skin where an oxygen mask and its straps rest?

question: What is the best way for a nurse leader to handle a transport breakdown during community outreach?

question: When should you wear medical gloves while caring for a patient?

question: Why is keeping our core body temperature within a steady, normal range so important?

question: When should the rehabilitation journey ideally start for a patient who has suffered a major injury?

question: A pregnant woman comes to the clinic for a routine checkup. What should the midwife focus on first?

question: Why is it better to call for an emergency medical assistance team early instead of waiting for a full cardiac arrest?

question: Which tocolytic drug is usually avoided past 32 weeks because it can affect the baby's heart circulation?

question: Why do our hands and fingers take up such a huge chunk of space on the motor homunculus?

options.C: They are closer to the brain than the lower extremities

question: What common barrier often affects contraceptive uptake in resource-constrained Nigerian communities?

question: A newborn has a heart rate of 110, pink body with blue hands, a strong cry, and pulls away when touched. What score do they get for muscle tone (Activity)?

options.B: Score of 2 for weak cry

question: What is the most important environmental requirement when screening a patient for gender-based violence?

question: A family is overwhelmed with funeral plans and hospital paperwork right after a death. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Tell them to figure it out since the patient is already gone

question: What is the biggest perk of using point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in emergency or acute care?

options.B: It requires no training for hospital staff to use

question: What is the main goal of giving medications for chronic, degenerative diseases like Parkinson's or Alzheimer's?

options.A: To manage ongoing physical and mental decline

options.D: To wipe out sudden bacterial infections in the tissues

question: Why is it much harder to set up strict transmission-based precautions in a home compared to a hospital?

options.A: Family members refuse to let nurses wear protective gear

options.C: Transmission-based precautions only work inside sterile laboratories
options.D: Homes lack negative pressure rooms and structural barriers

question: If a trauma patient's Glasgow Coma Scale score starts dropping over a couple of hours, what is the most likely reason?

options.A: Successful recovery from the primary injury

options.C: Worsening intracranial pressure or bleeding

question: You notice three people from the same street come to the clinic with severe watery diarrhea within 24 hours. What should you do next?

options.A: Report the cluster through disease surveillance channels
options.B: Wait until ten more patients arrive before taking action
options.C: Advise them to buy over-the-counter painkillers
options.D: Discharge them immediately with oral rehydration advice

question: Which microscopic blood vessels act as the primary control valves for blood entering capillary beds?

options.A: Capillaries

explanation: Arterioles have smooth muscle walls that constrict or dilate to control the volume of blood flowing into local capillary networks. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why is being kind and compassionate so important when caring for a PAC patient?

options.A: It prevents the physical pain caused by uterine contractions

options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any antibiotic therapy

question: What is the medical term for an infection in the muscular middle layer of the heart?

options.A: Endocarditis

options.D: Epicarditis

question: What special food product is lifesaver for treating severe malnutrition in emergencies?

options.A: High-sodium carbonated soft drinks
options.B: Ready-to-use therapeutic foods (RUTF)
options.C: Frozen commercial beef burgers
options.D: Standard multi-vitamin tablet bottles

question: What type of lubricant should you always use when inserting a rectal medication?

options.A: Petroleum-based grease

options.C: Alcohol-based sanitizer
options.D: Water-soluble lubricant

question: What is the main reason we tell postpartum mothers to drink plenty of fluids and eat high-fiber foods?

options.A: To stop painful uterine afterpains
options.B: To turn lochia serosa into lochia rubra
options.C: To shrink the size of the bladder

question: Why is the middle part (midpiece) of a sperm packed with mitochondria?

options.A: To store extra genetic material for embryonic development after fertilization
options.B: To generate the ATP energy needed to power the flagellum for swimming
options.C: To synthesize testosterone required for maintaining sperm motility

question: Why can minor physiological disturbances quickly become dangerous in critically ill patients?

options.A: Hospital rooms are usually too cold for recovery.
options.B: Their organ systems are already operating near total failure.
options.C: Laboratory tests are rarely accurate in acute settings.
options.D: Intravenous lines frequently disconnect by themselves.

explanation: When organs have little reserve left, even a small stressor can tip the patient over the edge into complete system failure. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h1)

question: A patient with Addison's disease gets a severe stomach infection and comes to the ER very weak, confused, and with dangerously low blood pressure. What is happening?

options.A: Cushing's syndrome
options.B: Addisonian crisis
options.C: Pheochromocytoma storm
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

explanation: This is an emergency! When a physical stressor like an infection hits someone with Addison's, their body can crash into an Addisonian crisis due to a sudden lack of cortisol. Quick fluids and steroids save lives here. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T12#GNS222_U2_T12_h3)

question: A patient in Buck's extension says their heel feels like it is burning under the foam boot. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Inspect the skin under the boot for redness or pressure damage
options.B: Permanently cut off the traction straps without telling anyone
options.C: Add an extra weight to the rope to lift the heel higher
options.D: Administer a strong sleeping pill to help ignore the sensation

question: What is the main goal of doing a home visit when assessing family vulnerability?

options.A: To search the house for stolen property
options.B: To check out environmental hazards and living conditions firsthand
options.C: To collect local government taxes from the residents
options.D: To force the family to sweep their yard immediately

question: Why is addressing emotional and mental health considered essential in rehabilitative care?

options.A: Mental health support can reverse genetic mutations in the brain

options.C: Emotional distress can worsen physical symptoms and reduce coping
options.D: Families do not require any support until the final stages of illness

explanation: Mental and emotional health directly impacts a patient's willingness and ability to participate in rehabilitation and enjoy daily life. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical barrier to effective nursing counselling?

options.A: Patient mistrust of healthcare workers
options.B: Having too much uninterrupted personal time

options.D: Severe time constraints in busy clinics

question: A patient says they can't follow their diabetic meal plan because fresh veggies are too expensive in their area. What is your best first nursing move?

options.B: Advise the patient to stop eating vegetables entirely and take vitamin pills
options.C: Explore affordable alternatives like frozen or canned vegetables and consult social work
options.D: Tell the patient that buying fresh vegetables is mandatory for survival

question: Which psychological condition is commonly reported among survivors of FGM?

options.D: Bipolar manic depression exclusively

question: What is the main difference between the ureters and the urethra?

question: Why does setting up a predictable daily routine help a home care client dealing with mental health struggles?

options.B: It completely cures chronic physical diseases

question: What is the main reason nurses use screening tools like the CAGE questionnaire?

question: Why do vitamin and mineral shortages happen so easily in people living with HIV?

question: Who should standard precautions be applied to in a healthcare setting?

question: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes insists on a strict all-day fast. What is the major clinical risk to watch for?

question: What is the number one risk factor for developing a placenta accreta?

question: A hospital pays great salaries, but nurses keep resigning. What should management look at next?

question: Which group of people is diagnosed with disseminated sclerosis more often?

question: Why do critical care medications require exceptionally close monitoring by the nurse?

question: What is the main focus of a nurse's day-to-day role in neurological care?

question: Which room adjustment helps prevent falls on indoor steps for someone with low vision?

question: What usually happens when health professionals bypass community input and decide problems alone?

question: How do clinic registers help nurses identify children who have defaulted?

question: What is the main goal of a safe injection according to the WHO?

question: What does an operating budget typically cover for a nursing unit?

question: What is a key clinical responsibility of a community health nurse managing tuberculosis (TB) patients?

question: What is the main benefit of placing a patient in the lateral (side-lying) position?

question: A client with severe high blood pressure requests a combined oral contraceptive pill. What is the most appropriate nursing action based on safety guidelines?

question: What term describes the process of putting displaced bone fragments back into their normal alignment?

question: A confused elderly patient is admitted to the ward. Which temperature route is safest and most appropriate for initial assessment?

question: Why would a doctor choose an MRI over a standard X-ray for a patient?

question: A patient is scared and hesitant to tell their partner about a new STI diagnosis. As a nurse, how should you help?

question: How does the team nursing setup benefit junior staff and nursing students on the ward?

question: What does nutritional literacy refer to?

question: Why is an injection considered a high-risk procedure despite its daily frequency?

question: In the handy PQRSTU pain assessment tool, what does the letter 'Q' stand for?

question: What immediate emergency action should you take if the chest tube accidentally pulls loose from the drainage machine?

question: What is the main danger of leaving a collected lab specimen sitting at room temperature for too long?

question: Which of the following is recognized as a harmful traditional practice?

question: How do subjective and objective data team up during patient assessment?

options.C: Subjective data provides history while objective data provides measurable findings
options.D: Subjective and objective data are completely unrelated processes

explanation: Think of it this way: subjective data is what the patient tells you (like 'my head hurts'), while objective data is what you measure or see yourself (like a high temperature). Together, they give the full picture! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h1)

question: What problem is a varicocele repair surgery designed to fix in men?

options.A: Infection in the prostate gland
options.B: A hormonal imbalance in the pituitary gland
options.C: Enlarged veins in the scrotum that warm the testes
options.D: A complete lack of sperm production in the bone marrow

explanation: Varicoceles trap heat in the scrotum, which hurts sperm. Repairing them cools things down and helps sperm grow healthy again! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T23#GNS312_U1_T23_h5)

question: What is a major limitation of using radio broadcasts for community health education?

options.A: It can only be used inside hospital wards
options.B: It completely replaces the need for clinical nurses
options.C: It is impossible for illiterate people to ever hear a radio
options.D: It lacks two-way interaction and personalized feedback

explanation: While radio reaches many people, listeners can't ask questions right away or get personalized answers the way they can with a nurse present. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the final step in the core disease surveillance cycle?

options.A: Collecting more patient samples
options.B: Archiving reports in a cabinet
options.C: Destroying old laboratory records
options.D: Taking public health action

explanation: Data collection and analysis are useless unless they lead directly to meaningful public health action and control measures. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: A new trauma patient is struggling to breathe and has no breath sounds on the right side. Using ABCDE, what is your next step after checking the airway?

options.A: Breathing
options.B: Disability
options.C: Circulation
options.D: Exposure

explanation: We always follow the strict ABCDE order. Once the airway (A) is clear, breathing (B) is your immediate next focus! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is a common cultural view in some Nigerian communities that affects family planning?

options.A: Children born in large numbers are automatically given free education
options.B: Large family sizes are seen as a sign of wealth and prestige
options.C: Small families are forbidden by ancestral spirits
options.D: Contraception is required by traditional law for all couples

explanation: In many cultures, having many children is traditionally viewed as a great blessing and a symbol of high status, which can make people hesitant about birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h3)

question: What happens if a nurse forgets to push the foreskin back down after cleaning an uncircumcised male patient?

options.A: Paraphimosis and painful swelling of the penis
options.B: Permanent loss of bladder control
options.C: Total blockage of urine flow
options.D: A fast fungal infection on the legs

explanation: Spot on! Leaving the foreskin pulled back acts like a tight rope, cutting off blood flow and causing a painful swelling called paraphimosis. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the main mindset shift behind trauma-informed care?

options.A: Asking what happened to the patient instead of what is wrong with them
options.B: Minimizing emotional expressions to maintain clinical efficiency
options.C: Determining the legal guilt of the alleged perpetrator immediately
options.D: Focusing exclusively on surgical repair of physical wounds

explanation: Instead of judging a patient's behavior, trauma-informed care reminds us to ask, 'What happened to you?' It's all about empathy. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h5)

question: What should the nurse check when inspecting the dressing after the procedure?

options.A: Whether the skin has turned a pale yellow color
options.B: If the adhesive tape is completely waterproof
options.C: Signs of bleeding, swelling, or fluid leakage
options.D: The exact temperature of the bandage material

explanation: Spot on! Regular site checks ensure any bleeding or fluid leakage is caught and managed early. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h6)

question: How should chronic pain medication be scheduled for a palliative care patient?

options.A: Only when the patient cries out in pain
options.B: Around the clock to maintain steady relief
options.C: Only when vital signs begin to spike
options.D: Strictly once every 24 hours in the morning

explanation: Giving pain meds around the clock prevents pain from spiking wildly and keeps the patient consistently comfortable. Simple and effective nursing care! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h3)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in public health projects?

options.A: Monitoring costs a lot of money, while evaluation is completely free
options.B: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring is continuous tracking, while evaluation measures final outcomes against objectives
options.D: Monitoring focuses on finance, while evaluation focuses entirely on building roads

explanation: Monitoring happens all through the project to keep things on track, whereas evaluation looks back to see if goals were met. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h9)

question: During early preeclampsia, what goes wrong with the blood vessels supplying the placenta?

options.A: They fail to widen and stay too narrow.
options.B: They wander completely away from the placenta.
options.C: They burst and cause heavy internal bleeding.
options.D: They multiply too fast and block blood flow.

explanation: Normally, these spiral arteries open up wide to feed the baby. When they stay tight and narrow, the placenta gets stressed from lack of blood flow, kicking off preeclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h2)

question: Which condition is a clear indication for using a warm poultice?

options.A: A widespread whole-body viral fever
options.B: A brand new ankle sprain with active bleeding
options.C: A localized boil or deep muscle ache
options.D: An area of skin with complete loss of sensation

explanation: Poultices work best on localized aches, stiffness, and closed infections like boils. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h4)

question: A nurse sets up a free blood pressure check at the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Primordial prevention

explanation: You nailed it! Secondary prevention is about catching health issues early through screening before they cause major trouble. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h3)
